records.name: Republic of Mordovia
records.current_summary: This division was covered by the dedicated country dossier, which identified no deviation from the national position material enough to score separately (±0.02); it is therefore assessed at the national score.

sources.claim: UK Home Office country policy and information note on Russia, SOGI (June 2025): same-sex sexual activity is not criminalised, but same-sex marriage and gender transition are banned, gender-marker changes on documents are prohibited, and trans-specific healthcare was effectively banned in 2023; the 2013 'gay propaganda' law is punishable by administrative fines or detention up to 15 days, escalating to up to four years' imprisonment on repeat offence, and since the 2023 'extremist' designation of the international LGBT+ movement, participation carries 2-6 years and organising 6-10 years' imprisonment. Records at least 139 people in Russia impacted by anti-LGBT+ laws between 2022 and 2024 and assesses that openly LGBT+ people face societal discrimination that may amount to persecution, the state able but unwilling to protect. The national framework this record claims (assessed at the national score; no regional deviation identified).

Human Rights Watch (30 Jun 2025): Russian courts have issued 101 'extremism'-related convictions (about 98 administrative, 3 criminal) for alleged participation in the 'International LGBT Movement' or displaying its symbols since the 2023 Supreme Court 'extremist' designation; between January 2024 and June 2025 at least 20 people faced criminal charges, including three publishing-house staff charged under article 282.2 who face up to 12 years' imprisonment, and 81 people were convicted in 98 administrative cases under article 20.3 for displaying banned symbols. Documents the national enforcement wave whose score this record adopts, with no region-specific deviation identified.
